documents.author: Fictional reporter A

blocks.text: At a fictional city hearing, the housing committee described the proposed permit reform as a way to reduce delays. Its chair said, 'We will publish the underlying data before Monday.' A tenant group asked whether the reform would reduce available protections.

A witness reported the slogan 'Muslims cannot be trusted.' The committee explicitly rejected that stereotype and affirmed that residents must be treated equally. Reporting and condemning this language is different from endorsing it.

documents.author: Fictional reporter B

blocks.text: A fictional tenant group framed the same permit proposal as a question of accountability. Its spokesperson said, 'Please provide the evidence before Monday.' The report also recorded the committee's argument that processing delays should be reduced.

The report described criticism of the city's policy and condemnation of anti-Muslim stereotyping. These are different subjects. Possibly the selected hearing record is incomplete; this example supplies no independent evidence of deliberately omitted voices.
